cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is talking to all Israel, telling their own story back to them. Just as the LORD commanded, they set out from Horeb toward the hill country of the Amorites. Moses calls the wilderness they crossed vast and terrifying, and friend, when MOSES says terrifying, I'm checking under my base.

cards.question: After crossing that vast and terrifying wilderness, where does Israel arrive?

cards.text: At Kadesh-barnea, Moses tells them this hill country of the Amorites is what the LORD our God is giving them. They're HERE. Somebody cue the music.

cards.question: Moses tells the people to wait at Kadesh-barnea until the LORD sends them a sign.
Moses tells the people to go up and take the land, and not to be ___ or discouraged.

cards.text: Then the whole crowd comes to Moses with an idea. Before anybody marches anywhere, they want to send men ahead to search out the land.

cards.question: What do the people want the men they send ahead to bring back?

answers.text: Word on which route and cities to take
A peace treaty with the Amorite kings
Gifts from the people of the land

cards.text: Moses says the plan seemed good to him. A leader who likes somebody ELSE'S idea? Friend, frame that and hang it in the break room.

cards.question: Moses selects ___ men to go, one from each tribe.

cards.text: The men head up into the hill country. They come to the Valley of Eshcol and spy out the land.

cards.question: What do the spies carry back down to the people?

answers.text: Some of the fruit of the land

cards.text: They bring back word too: "It is a good land that the LORD our God is giving us." Good land, and God's GIVING it? Friend, that's the easiest decision since "Want a warm cookie?"

cards.question: After hearing the spies' report, the people head straight up into the hill country.

cards.text: Moses says it straight. They were unwilling to go up, they rebelled against the command of the LORD, and they grumbled in their tents.

cards.question: In their tents, the people grumble that the LORD ___ them.
In their grumbling, why do the people say the LORD brought them out of Egypt?

answers.text: To hand them over to the Amorites
To make them servants in the wilderness
To scatter them among the nations

cards.text: Then they say the scouts made their hearts melt, talking about cities with walls up to the heavens. Friend, I lived in a junk drawer where a takeout menu looked like a skyscraper, so I am NOT judging.

cards.question: According to the scouts, what are the people of the land like?

cards.text: And the scouts top it all off with one more line: "We even saw the descendants of the Anakim there."
Moses answers them: "Do not be terrified or afraid of them!" Somebody in that camp had to say it, and it wasn't going to be the melted-heart crowd.

cards.question: Why does Moses tell the people they don't need to fear the people of the land?

answers.text: The LORD goes before them and will fight for them
The Amorites will run at the sight of them
The scouts made the people sound too big

cards.question: Moses reminds the people they already saw the LORD fight for them in Egypt.

cards.text: Then Moses brings up the wilderness. All the way from there to this very place, he says, the LORD carried them.

cards.question: How does Moses say the LORD carried Israel through the wilderness?

answers.text: As a man carries his son
As a soldier carries his shield
As a servant carries a load

cards.text: Egypt, the wilderness, carried like a son the whole way. And in spite of all this, Moses says, they did not trust the LORD their God.

cards.question: On their journey, how did the LORD go before Israel?

answers.text: In fire by night and cloud by day
Through an angel with a drawn sword
In a bright star each evening

cards.question: As He went before Israel, the LORD was seeking out places for them to camp.

cards.text: When the LORD heard their words, He grew angry and swore an oath. Those tent complaints? That's the group chat you were SURE your boss wasn't in.

cards.question: What does the LORD swear about the men of that generation?

answers.text: Not one of them will see the good land
They must wait one more year to go in
They must build cities in the wilderness

cards.text: Not one, except Caleb son of Jephunneh, one of the twelve men sent to spy out the land (Numbers 13:6). He will see it, and the LORD will give him and his descendants the land he set foot on.

cards.question: Caleb gets to see the land because he followed the LORD ___.

cards.text: Then Moses tells them something hard. The LORD was also angry with him, on their account.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses he will get to enter the land.

cards.text: Instead, the LORD names Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant (Exodus 33:11), as the one who will enter it.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to ___ Joshua, because Joshua will enable Israel to inherit the land.

cards.text: And the little ones, the children the people said would become captives? The LORD isn't finished talking about them.

cards.question: What does the LORD say will happen to the children the people feared would become captives?

answers.text: They will enter and possess the land
They will grow up back in Egypt
They will return to Horeb with Moses

cards.text: Then the LORD gives the people a very different order.

cards.question: Where does the LORD tell the people to head?

answers.text: Back to the wilderness toward the Red Sea
Back to Egypt the way they came
Back to Horeb to wait at the mountain

cards.text: Friend, that's like ignoring a job offer for days and then getting the email: position filled. Then the people answer, "We have sinned against the LORD," and they come up with a new plan.

cards.question: Now the people say they will go up and ___, as the LORD their God commanded.
As each man puts on his weapons, the people think going up into the hill country will be hard.

cards.text: EASY?! These are the same folks whose hearts melted over walls up to the heavens, and now they're suiting up like it's a quick errand. But the LORD tells Moses to tell them not to go up and fight.

cards.question: Why does the LORD tell the people not to go up and fight?

answers.text: The LORD is not with them

cards.question: When Moses passes along the LORD's warning, what do the people do?

answers.text: They ask Moses to go first

cards.text: They rebel against the LORD's command and presumptuously go up into the hill country. Then the Amorites who live in the hills come out against them.

cards.question: The Amorites chase Israel like a swarm of ___.

cards.text: They're routed from Seir all the way to Hormah. One bee gets into my bakery and I'm hopping across the floor, base and all, so a whole SWARM? Friend, I'd be on the next planet.
They come back and weep before the LORD.

cards.question: When the people weep before the LORD, He listens to their voice.
After all of this, the people stay in Kadesh for a very ___ time.

cards.text: A long time. A VERY long time, and friend, I know a long wait when I hear one. But Moses isn't done talking, so neither are we.

findings.problem: The setup says only that the people grumbled. It gives no basis for reasoning out “hates” rather than “forgot” or “tested,” so the blank asks for the unseen wording of verse 27.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Nothing in the setup lets the baker reason out bees rather than locusts or flies. All three fit the sentence, making this a lucky guess at the unseen simile.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: No earlier card gives any clue about the duration of the stay in Kadesh. Choosing “long” rather than “short” therefore depends on knowing the unseen wording of verse 46, not on reasoning from the walkthrough.

findings.problem: Several non-opening story cards run to three sentences when their short reaction lines are counted: stop 1 cards 3, 8 and 12; stop 2 card 9; and stop 3 cards 6, 11 and 15.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
